MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  OCTOBER 10, 2017

MAYOR ZERUNYAN called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. and the City Council convened
into closed session in the City Manager’s office, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills
Estates, CA.

City Council Members Present: Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  Mitchell (excused)

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Planning Director David Wahba

14.  CLOSED SESSION (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER)

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Significant exposure to litigation under Government Code Section
  54956.9(d)(2): one case

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

B.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Title: City Manager (Quarterly Evaluation)
  Government Code Section 54957

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

  ***

At 7:13 p.m., the COUNCIL reconvened in open session in the City Council Chamber, 4045
Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, CA.

  ***

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman.

City Council Members Absent:  Mitchell (excused)

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
OCTOBER 10, 2017
 City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Alexa Davis, Assistant to the City Manager led the audience in the Pledge of Allegiance.

CEREMONIAL ITEMS

NONE.

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 26, 2017 – 4:00 P.M.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO APPROVE THE ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 26,
  2017 – 4:00 P.M. AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

B.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 26, 2017 – 5:00 P.M.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 26, 2017 – 5:00
  P.M. AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 26, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN.

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 26, 2017 AS
  PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
OCTOBER 10, 2017
 D.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – SEPTEMBER AND OCTOBER

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 59012 THROUGH 59034 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $39,183.30; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 090117 THROUGH 090717;
  58888 THROUGH 58890; 58932 THROUGH 58964; 59002 THROUGH 59011 IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $319,671,17 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF
  $358,854.47 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
  consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless
  good cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be
  considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF.

  TO APPROVE ITEMS A-B.

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the
  City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by
  title only.

  APPROVED.

B.  RESOLUTION NO. 2409 AFFIRMING THE FISCAL YEAR 2017-2018 BUDGET FOR
  USE OF FUNDS PROVIDED BY THE ROAD REPAIR AND ACCOUNTABILITY ACT OF
  2017 (SB-1)

  ADOPTED AS PRESENTED.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Resolution No. 2409 by title only.

7.  AUDIENCE  ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

Resident Paul Moylan addressed the City Council to express concern regarding traffic during
California Water Service Company’s upcoming pipeline realignment project on Palos Verdes
Drive North near Dapplegray Lane; and to suggest that the City pursue undergrounding of
the utilities in conjunction with this project.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 10, 2017
 MAYOR ZERUNYAN commented that the City did inquire about the ability to underground
the utilities as part of the project, but was told that doing so was not a feasible option.

Mr. Moylan also suggested that the City contact the City of Lomita to address the street
striping on Narbonne Avenue where it crosses Pacific Coast Highway and merges to one lane.
In response to Mr. Moylan’s concern, City Manager Prichard stated that staff would contact
the City of Lomita to see if anything can be done to address the issue.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

  NONE

9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 22-17; PROPOSAL FROM ROBERT SPENCER (DBA
  URBAN ECONOMICS) TO PREPARE AN UPDATE TO THE CITY’S DEVELOPMENT
  IMPACT FEE PROGRAM

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize approval of a Professional Services
  Agreement (PSA) with Robert Spencer, dba Urban Economics, in the amount of
  $30,000 to prepare an update to the City’s Development Impact Fee program.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ regarding the term of the plan, Robert
  Spencer from Urban Economics stated that the plan will be updated based on SCAG’s
  projections – likely through 2035 or 2040 and determining the term will be one of the
  first task undertaken with staff.

  Also in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ regarding the growth projections,
  Mr. Spencer commented that he can look at the numbers compared to the 2007
  projections, but those numbers will not impact most of the fees being evaluated. He
  further commented that the fees being evaluated, typically track with the growth so
  the population projections are not critically important.

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding hotel fees, Mr. Spencer
  commented that under the Mitigation Fee Act, a relationship has to be drawn between
  the impact of the land use and the fee that would be paid and the use of the fee
  revenue for a public facility to address those impacts.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF.

  TO AUTHORIZE APPROVAL OF A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
  (PSA) WITH ROBERT SPENCER, DBA URBAN ECONOMICS, IN AN AMOUNT
  NOT TO EXCEED $30,000 TO PREPARE AN UPDATE TO THE CITY’S
  DEVELOPMENT IMPACT FEE PROGRAM.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
OCTOBER 10, 2017
 B.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF JULY
  31, 2017 - CITY-OWNED LED STREETLIGHTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the following: 1) retrofitting all
  City-owned streetlights to LED lamps; 2) the City to submit an application for
  Southern California Edison’s on bill financing to finance the project; 3) the City to
  submit an application for Southern California Edison’ streetlight incentives; 4) staff to
  proceed with bidding the project in coordination with the South Bay Cities Council of
  Governments; 5) City funds in the amount of $3,500 to be used toward this project.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material)
  and reviewed a PowerPoint presentation.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding the background on City
  ownership vs. SCE ownership of the streetlights, Assistant to the City Manager Davis
  stated that there is not much history available on that matter; and several cities are
  going through a process of purchasing the SCE owned streetlights.

  In response to MAYOR ZERUNYAN regarding SCE’s ON BILL financing program,
  Assistant to the City Manager Davis stated that the variable will be the amount
  financed and the availability of SCE’s streetlight incentives.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO AUTHORIZE THE FOLLOWING: 1) RETROFITTING ALL CITY-OWNED
  STREETLIGHTS TO LED LAMPS; 2) THE CITY TO SUBMIT AN APPLICATION
  FOR SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA EDISON’S ON BILL FINANCING TO FINANCE
  THE PROJECT; 3) THE CITY TO SUBMIT AN APPLICATION FOR SOUTHERN
  CALIFORNIA EDISON’ STREETLIGHT INCENTIVES; 4) STAFF TO PROCEED
  WITH BIDDING THE PROJECT IN COORDINATION WITH THE SOUTH BAY
  CITIES COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS; 5) CITY FUNDS IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $3,500 TO BE USED TOWARD THIS PROJECT.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

10.  OLD BUSINESS

  NONE

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

  NONE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
OCTOBER 10, 2017
 12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:  This item provides the
  opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to other
  Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of currently
  active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide governmental
  associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and their various
  committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or have an interest, which
  are not otherwise agendized.

A.  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE COMMITTEE MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 25, 2017 –
  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF AND COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF reported that the Grand Marshalls for this year’s parade will
  be Jackie Crowley who was selected by the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of
  Commerce Citizen of the Year and Tracy Austin as the Celebrity Grand Marshall.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE COMMITTEE
  MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 25, 2017 AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

B.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 25, 2017 – COUNCIL
  MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN.

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF
  SEPTEMBER 25, 2017 AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF reported that the SBCCOG Steering Committee agreed to review the
methodology used in setting the dues structure. MAYOR ZERUNYAN suggested that the City
Manager participate in the review process and that expenses be evaluated as well.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF also reported that the SBCCOG/LOCC Legislative Breakfast at the
Nakano Theater is scheduled for December 13. She also noted that Larry Kosmont is
confirmed as a speaker for the SBCCOG General Assembly meeting in February 2017.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ reiterated the importance of having the SBCCOG dues issue
resolved prior to the Policy Development Session and/or prior to making a budget decision
on this issue for fiscal year 2018/19.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF thanked Community Services Director Clark for his efforts in
spearheading the Romanian Festival that was held this past weekend. MAYOR ZERUNYAN
commented that the festival organizers were very impressed with the community, the City’s
park facility and the support that City staff provided.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
OCTOBER 10, 2017
 COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN reported that LACCE has hired staff to commence the first
phase of the program for the County, with the second phase to follow in approximately six
month.

13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members of the
  City Council to request information on currently pending projects and/or issues of public
  concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration and/or make
  announcements of interest to the public.

  NONE

14.  CLOSED SESSION

  TAKEN OUT OF ORDER – SEE ABOVE

15.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 8:02 p.m. MAYOR ZERUNYAN formally adjourned the City Council meeting in
  memory of the victims of last week’s senseless tragedy in Las Vegas, NV to an
  adjourned City Council meeting of October 24, 2017 at 5:00 p.m. for the purpose of
  conducting a City Council Workshop on Group Dynamics and Communication.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Douglas R. Prichard
City Clerk  City Manager

OCTOBER 10, 2017
